entries.what: Gemini's Narrowneck dossier (two stacked 'inshore' + 'offshore' lobes, 400 x 220 m, 75,000 m2) and its sources
entries.where: Gemini folder (read-only): reef_footprints.json; its cited sources Black and Mead 2001, Jackson et al. 2012, ICM webinar (Salyer 2025), Swellnet 2017-11-07, Wikimedia photo
entries.detail: No source supports the lobes or the 400 x 220 m / 75,000 m2 figures. Jackson et al. 2012 (our PDF) shows two alongshore arms with a central channel / weir and flared wings and contains no such figure; the ICM page and webinar slide (registry img-42) show the reef but give no dimensions or levels; Black and Mead 2001 is paywalled. Swellnet 2017-11-07 is correct only as a depth quote (2.5-2.6 m at low tide), not a plan source. The Gemini hosts could not be re-fetched from the cloud (WebFetch ENOTFOUND; swellnet 2019-08-19 timed out). Gemini lead not confirmed; nothing used.

entries.what: Esri Wayback releases of Narrowneck for 2012-07-03 (release 10) and 2014-08-02 (release 6984), and the 2025-10-10 release (22869) at z19
entries.detail: HTTP 404 on the z19 tile for releases 6984 and 10 (z19 not served for them; z18 retry not recorded). The 2025-10 tile is featureless. The 2022-23 and 2025-04 tiles match 2020-08-08 to 0.2 m; the 2016-07-01 pre-renewal frame is murky (south arm further 55 m of containers either added or uncovered, unresolved). The seaward toe in -6 to -10 m and three seaward dark patches are not visible in any frame, so the footprint is a lower bound.
entries.might_work: Google Earth Pro historical imagery (Lior: G6); City's multibeam (E3); the 2025 State bathymetric LiDAR if released

entries.what: Garmin / Navionics SonarChart and Nautical chart at Narrowneck for the crest level and nearshore bed (registry img-50 to img-53)
entries.detail: The crowd-sourced SonarChart shows the reef only as shoals 1.5-2 m above the 5.5-6 m seabed (4.0-4.5 m contours) and cannot resolve a crest at -1.4 m LAT. Its land edge lies about 80 m seaward of the 2020-08-08 waterline, so the nearshore contours were not used. The nautical layer gives only spot depths 0.9 (suffix unclear, datum unstated, probably an older crest state of 1.0 m below LAT) and 5.9 in a restricted-area polygon, no reef outline. Only the seaward bed (y 385-500 m) was taken from it.
entries.might_work: Lior: Navionics app readings (REQUESTS section 5, Narrowneck rows: the '0.9' label and four points off the beach)

entries.detail: Airborne bathymetric LiDAR (1 m DEM, 200 m onshore to up to 6 km offshore, AHD; flown from mid-July 2025) is free to councils but 'no decision on public availability' (Sultmann 2025). Only the Sunshine Coast 2011-12 pilot is open; older Queensland data are 'up to 40 years old' surveys of uncertain accuracy. No open-coast Gold Coast beach-profile, multibeam or LiDAR layer was found in QSpatial / Queensland Globe / AusSeabed / GCWA / MSQ. The qcoast2100.com.au PDF gave 403 to scripts; the copy cached by WebFetch was read.
